title: Random Name Picker Wheel | ToolsBuilt
description: Free online random name picker wheel. Enter names, spin to select unbiased winners for raffles, classrooms, and giveaways. Powered by Web Crypto API.
quickAnswer: To pick a random name or winner from a list, paste or type your candidates, choose whether to remove duplicates, and click pick. The tool uses cryptographically secure hardware randomness to ensure equal winning probability without bias. It supports single-winner draws and multi-prize raffles without replacement.

formula.title: Fair Selection & Probability Formula
formula.expression: P(Selection) = 1 / Total Candidate Pool Size  |  Index = CryptoRandomUint() % PoolSize
formula.explanation: Every candidate possesses a mathematically identical probability of selection. Drawing uses native browser Web Crypto API hardware entropy with rejection sampling to eliminate modulo bias. For multi-tier raffles without replacement, selected winners are removed sequentially from the pool.

commonMistakes.title: Using Predictable Math.random() in Real Contests
commonMistakes.description: Standard pseudo-random Math.random() is susceptible to statistical patterns. Giveaways require cryptographic hardware randomness via crypto.getRandomValues.

commonMistakes.title: Allowing Accidental Duplicate Entries
commonMistakes.description: When pasting entries from spreadsheets, duplicate names double an entrant's winning odds. Always use the Deduplicate button before spinning.

commonMistakes.title: Drawing With Replacement in Tiered Giveaways
commonMistakes.description: Failing to remove previous winners during multi-prize draws allows the same participant to win multiple prizes.

commonMistakes.title: Modulo Skew in Candidate Indexing
commonMistakes.description: Simple modulo operations on random integers introduce slight mathematical bias toward lower index values. Rejection sampling ensures exact uniform fairness.

howto.name: How to Pick a Random Name Using the Wheel
howto.description: Step-by-step instructions for selecting random winners using cryptographically unbiased wheel spins.

steps.name: Enter Participant Names
steps.text: Type or paste your list of names into the text box (one name per line, or comma-separated).

steps.name: Configure Settings
steps.text: Optionally click Deduplicate to remove duplicate entries, or check 'Remove winner automatically after spin' for multi-round draws.

steps.name: Spin Wheel to Pick Winner
steps.text: Click Spin Wheel to initiate the spin animation or instant selection if reduced motion is preferred.

steps.name: Announce and Copy Winner
steps.text: View the winning name in the modal announcement dialog and copy the winner's name to your clipboard.

faqs.q: How does the random name picker ensure fair and unbiased selection?
faqs.a: The tool utilizes your browser's native Web Crypto API via crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling to eliminate modulo bias. Unlike standard Math.random algorithms, hardware-level OS entropy ensures uniform probability distribution across all entries. Every name has an equal mathematical chance of being chosen on each spin.

faqs.q: Can I remove winning names automatically after each spin?
faqs.a: Yes. Simply enable the 'Remove winner automatically after spin' checkbox, or click 'Remove Winner & Close' in the announcement modal. The tool removes the chosen entry immediately and redraws the wheel geometry for subsequent rounds.

faqs.q: Does the wheel accommodate users with motion sensitivity or vestibular disorders?
faqs.a: Yes. The random name picker respects your device's system-level accessibility preferences. When 'prefers-reduced-motion' is active, spinning animations are bypassed entirely. The tool computes the winning slice instantly and opens the winner dialog immediately.

faqs.q: Is there a limit on how many names I can paste into the wheel?
faqs.a: You can enter hundreds of names into the text box. The generator automatically calculates slice angles and fits labels on the wheel. Each slice remains mathematically distinct throughout the cryptographic selection process.

faqs.q: Are my participant names stored on remote servers or tracked?
faqs.a: No. All name lists, spin computations, and winner selections operate exclusively in local browser memory. None of your entered names are transmitted to external servers, logged in databases, or stored in URLs.

faqs.q: Can I paste comma-separated or semicolon-separated names?
faqs.a: Yes. The input parser splits entries automatically across newlines, commas, and semicolons, trimming extra whitespace around each name.

faqs.q: How do I ensure fair odds when multiple tickets per person are allowed?
faqs.a: Leave the Deduplicate option unchecked so entrants who purchased multiple tickets retain their multiple entries in the candidate pool.

why-use-a-digital-random-name.heading: Why Use a Digital Random Name Picker Wheel?
why-use-a-digital-random-name.p1: Whether you are running a social media giveaway, choosing students for classroom participation, organizing team secret Santa exchanges, or deciding who pays for coffee, choosing fairly is essential. Physical drawings with paper slips take time to assemble and can raise suspicions of bias. Digital spinning wheels provide a transparent, engaging, and verifiably fair method for picking winners in real time.

cryptographically-secure-randomness.heading: Cryptographically Secure Randomness
cryptographically-secure-randomness.p1: Many online wheels rely on standard pseudorandom number generators like Math.random(), which are fine for basic games but exhibit predictable mathematical patterns over repeated runs. Our tool utilizes the browser's native Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues). This provides hardware-level entropy and cryptographically strong randomness, guaranteeing that every single spin is completely independent and unbiased.
